sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Ever-young Miquella watered the roots with his sacred Empyrean blood, producing a sapling that would become the Haligtree. Malenia, Blade of Miquella, locked in a deep slumber since her first bloom in Caelid, arrived here on the back of heroic Cleanrot Knight Finlay. Mohg, Lord of Blood cut Miquella from the cocoon and abducted him, carrying his slumbering body to the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum.

This location is the boss arena for Malenia, Blade of Miquella. The site of grace is unlocked after defeating Malenia, Goddess of Rot. Malenia's second rotflower bloom also appears after the player reloads the area, shielding the Empyrean slumbering within.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Libra, Creature of Night** (夜の魔、リブラ, *Yoru no Ma, Ribura*), also known as **Equilibrius Beast** (調律の魔物, *Chouritsu no Mamono*), is a Night Lord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Libra is a capricious, goat-headed demon obsessed with equality and fairness. He disguises himself as a Scale-Bearing Merchant and offers a deal before the fight. He offers three deals, pulled from a randomized pool. Each deal is a Monkey's Paw wish: it provides a powerful buff, but comes at a great cost. Players may decline to bargain or simply attack Libra outright.

- Libra deals Physical and Holy damage, and inflicts Madness buildup.
- He uses the Crossed Legs gesture to inflict Madness. He is shielded by a golden sphere when he meditates in this way. The barrier can be shattered through force or by destroying the nearby sigils.
 - If the orb is shattered, he loses control and rampages like a beast.
 - If he finishes channeling, he enters a more composed state.
- Its attacks sometimes generate tiny false-gold pieces. Collect them to reduce Madness buildup.
- When it uses the chanting attack that makes a goat eye icon appear over the Nightfarers, prioritize collecting the yellow embers to avoid the incoming Frenzy proc.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.markdown:
- Damage Types
 - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
 - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
 - A negative value ( ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
 - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
 - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Equilibrious Beast Expedition.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- When Libra starts pummeling the ground and summoning a Madness aura, run around and collect as many false-gold pieces around the arena as you can. Each one heals you a bit but most importantly, alleviates Madness buildup.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Internal name: **Baphomet**.
- His connection to dubious alchemy and counterfeit gold are likely a play on the fact that the Japanese word for western alchemy, 錬金術 (*Renkinjutsu*, lit. the art of refining gold) refers in modern parlance to hucksters making money through unethical means and scams.
- He wields his staff in his left hand. Making him the next unique left-handed character that Fromsoft puts in their games. There’s always at least one in each installment. That is, Iron Golem in Dark Souls 1, Fume Knight and Throne Watcher in Dark Souls 2, Old Demon King and Dancer of the Boreal Valley in Dark Souls 3, Ludwig in Bloodborne, and Messmer in Elden Ring. Artorias was also rumored to be left-handed, before his arm was shattered.
- His name, Libra, is the same as a star sign in Astrology. Its unique symbol is that of a balance/scale, and its gemstone is an Opal. Its most prominent traits are that of Balance, Diplomacy, Charm, Intelligence, and Fairness.
- Libra is referred to as a *Demon* (悪魔, *Akuma*), making him the first of his kind in the Elden Ring universe.
 - The demons of the Demon's Souls and Dark Souls universes are known as デモン (*Demon*) in the Japanese script, a simple transcription of the English word Demon, while Libra uses 悪魔 (*Akuma*), a Japanese word which refers to demons such as the buddhist Mara and Christian devil, tying into its links to Baphomet, a medieval Christian garbling of the name of the Islamic prophet, which was later attached to Éliphas Lévi's Sabbatic Goat, an iconic depiction of a goat-headed figure which formed the basis for Libra's design.
 - Libra's title in Japanese (夜の魔) directly calls him "Demon of Night".

sections.markdown: Maliketh, the Black Blade** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The ruined sanctum atop Crumbling Farum Azula is the boss arena for the Beast Clergyman and Maliketh, the Black Blade—Queen Marika's feared shadowbound beast. An ancient shrine for Beastmen, it contains statues of a hallowed scene: three wolves attend to a young Empyrean, kneeling in prayer, beneath the glowing depiction of a primordial Elden Ring. Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is its caretaker.

Defeating Maliketh unbinds the Rune of Death, also known as Destined Death, and finalizes the Cardinal Sin, unsealing the Erdtree by burning away its impenetrable thorns with black flame.

The Maliketh, the Black Blade site of grace is located in Crumbling Farum Azula. It can be reached by traveling southeast from the Beside the Great Bridge site of grace and climbing the ramp to the top, though the road is protected by a Draconic Tree Sentinel.

The site of grace appears inside the structure after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Miséricorde** is a dagger found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Found behind a fog wall that requires 1 Stonesword Key to open, near the roaming Grafted Scion inside Stormveil Castle and the elevator shortcut back up to the Rampart Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Has the highest critical multiplier in the game, at 140.
- Generally average or above average damage depending on the affinity used, but always the strongest dagger for Critical Attacks such as backstabbing or riposting. As such it's useful as a secondary weapon to be pulled out quickly, even when a build isn't focused on daggers.
 - Deals damage equivalent to a Colossal Weapon, for comparison.
 - This damage is strong enough that a riposte with a Fire affinity Miséricorde can oftentimes overwhelm the flat defences that often hold back split damage weapons, dealing strong damage (doesn't work as well on backstabs since the damage multiplier for them is lower).
- While it technically leans towards Dexterity it actually performs about as well on the Heavy affinity as the Keen affinity, technically better due to most daggers not working as well with Strength.
 - Actually the strongest pure Dexterity dagger with the Cold affinity and the strongest dagger period on the Occult affinity, but lacks the support of other Status Effects that other daggers such as the Bloodstained Dagger and Great Knife have.
 - Despite the general Dexterity tendency its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Main-gauche, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
- Somewhat stronger on lower stats than other daggers due to its higher base damage but lower scaling.
- The longest of all daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
 - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

 - "Dagger of Mercy" is a literal translation of the Japanese name.
- This weapon was popular among speedrunners before the heavy nerf to the Stance damage of Flame of the Redmanes (from 40 to 10), due to the power of its critical hits.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Morgott, the Omen King,** is a remembrance boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Leyndell, Royal Capital. He is **not** an optional boss and must be defeated to unlock Mountaintops of the Giants and progress the story.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Morgott was a direct offspring of Lord Godfrey and Queen Marika, and the rightful heir to their Golden Lineage. Despite his royal pedigree, he and his twin brother, Mohg, were born with accursed blood that caused tangled horns to sprout from their infant bodies. Once revered as divine aspect of the Crucible, these growths branded them as Omen spurned by the Erdtree and excluded from its grace. Though spared the painful excision of their horns, they were nonetheless banished to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. A Regal Omen Bairn was made in secret to honor Morgott in a long-standing tradition.

Unlike his twin, Morgott's devotion to the Erdtree never wavered. He renounced his omen blood, extracted a portion of it, and sealed it away. The blood that formed Morgott's Cursed Sword caused it to shimmer in shifting hues, and so he encased it in stone and wielded it like a cane. Several horns were removed from his brow line.

sections.heading: The Shattering
Game events
sections.markdown:
When the Tarnished returned, Morgott and his Night's Cavalry hunted them throughout the realm. Morgott first encounters the Tarnished at Stormgate, where he tests their mettle as Margit before allowing them to challenge Godrick for his Great Rune. Later, he ambushes the hero again by disguising a commoner as himself in the war-torn Capital Outskirts.

The Tarnished gains entrance to Leyndell, Royal Capital and challenges Morgott at the Elden Throne after claiming two shards of the Elden Ring. Denouncing the Tarnished and his siblings as willful traitors, Morgott launches his assault. As he falters during the battle, he unleashes his sealed curse to aid him, though he feels unbearable shame in doing so. Despite his efforts, he is ultimately defeated and stripped of his Great Rune.

Without his Rune, Morgott is freed from his curse, and transforms into an enfeebled old man. He warns the Tarnished the impenetrable thorns would bar them from becoming Elden Lord, just as they rejected him. After the Cardinal Sin and the release of the Rune of Death, Morgott was finally able to truly die. At the Ashen Capital, Godfrey returned just in time to find his son in his final moments, cradling him tenderly as Morgott's body crumbled into golden dust.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown: Melina and Dung Eater are both available as summons for this fight. For Dung Eater to be available, the player must have released him from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.markdown: Morgott is a highly aggressive and fast-moving enemy, chaining together attacks in rapid succession while leaving few openings. His curved sword inflicts blood loss on impact, while the holy armaments he summons deal holy damage. He has ranged attacks, such as his throwing knives and spear, and utilises jumps, cartwheels, and dashes to close or create distance.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.markdown: Once his health drops to 50%, Morgott performs an area of effect attack in which his cursed blood erupts from the ground. His blade becomes infused with his cursed blood, and he gains a number of bloodflame-based attacks. He may also summon golden blades that rain down from the sky.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles, aside from the throne which will break if hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Though a common characteristic on Misbegotten, Morgott is the only Omen to display the tail Crucible aspect.
- Morgott likely seized power during or in the aftermath of the First Defense of Leyndell. As Margit the Fell, he actively participated in the Second Defense of Leyndell.
- Morgott was known as **the Grace-Given**, presumably awarded grace for his loyalty and dedication to the Erdtree, despite being an Omen born without it. Ironically, he dismisses the player as "graceless" before their battle.
- His other title is **the Veiled Monarch** of Leyndell, an alias adopted to conceal his Omen heritage from the public. All of his appearances—whether participating in battle or hunting champions—were conducted under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.
- Morgott can summon spectral weapons during his fights, including the Treespear, Giant-Crusher, Erdsteel Dagger, and Carian Knight's Sword.
 - While the first three weapons are associated with the Erdtree, its warriors, or its nobility, the Carian Knight's Sword originates with the Carian Royal Family, a curious choice given their shared ties to night. This may imply Morgott once observed Carian Knights—perhaps the guards of visiting diplomats—or that he mastered the sword sorceries during the Shattering.
- Though he fought on the battlefield for the majority of his time as Elden Lord, Godfrey reveals he knew Morgott before their banishment. He likely made the tanglehorn bairn in secret to memorialize his son, an ancient hornsent practice.
 - The precious bairn has a tail and Morgott's general horn pattern. It is wrapped in a small cloak identical to the one he wears in game. It is obtained using the Remembrance of the Omen King and is the only Remembrance reward made to memorialize its subject.
- Until his defeat, Morgott's seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken prevents access to the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- Like Godrick the Grafted and other Demigods, Morgott remains alive after his defeat. He becomes an NPC that can be spoken to.

- There was a cut questline involving Shanehaight, a nobleman of the capital, who discovers the truth about their Veiled Monarch, much to their horror.
- Morgott's name may be inspired by , the alias of Melkor, the main and very first antagonist of 's .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Mohg, Lord of Blood** and **Mohg, the Omen** are Bosses in Elden Ring. **Luminary Mohg** is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and at the Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Mohg, also known as the Lord of Blood, was born of the Golden Lineage—the offspring of Queen Marika and Godfrey, First Elden Lord—and was the twin brother of Morgott. The twins were accursed Omen and, as a result, were confined and shackled to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell.

Unlike his brother, Mohg embraced his Omen blood. Deep underground, Mohg made contact with an Outer God known as the Formless Mother, who ignited his accursed blood with bloodflame, granting him powerful magic.

Mohg escaped confinement in the wake of the Shattering, claiming a Great Rune of the Elden Ring. He began establishing his domain from Mohgwyn Palace and recruiting followers, including his Sanguine Nobles and a murderous Tarnished known as the Bloody Fingers. Among these followers was Sir Ansbach, commander of the Pureblood Knights, and Varré, a war surgeon who was able to successfully tame Mohg's accursed blood.

Miquella the Unalloyed later embedded himself within his Haligtree in an attempt to shed his affliction. In this vulnerable and unguarded state, Mohg seized the opportunity to abduct him from the tree. Miquella was an Empyrean, thus having the potential of ascending to godhood; Mohg intended to raise Miquella to full godhood so that he may rule at his side as consort and take the role of Elden Lord. At some point during or after the abduction, Mohg was unknowingly enchanted by Miquella. The circumstances and timeline of this enchantment remain unclear.

After abducting Miquella, Mohg hibernated with him within the Cocoon of the Empyrean, and had his followers render offerings of blood, drenching its chamber in order to facilitate Miquella's awakening. But no matter how much of Miquella's bloody bedchamber Mohg tried to share, he would receive no response from the young empyrean.

During this time, Mohg largely escaped the notice of the Roundtable Hold, who were searching for clues as to his whereabouts.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.markdown:
Eventually, the Tarnished came to learn the location of Mohg's palace, where he had hidden alongside the stolen Miquella. When the Tarnished stumbles upon his chambers, Mohg emerges from a pool of blood, holds Miquella's hand and apologizes for leaving him, ready to confront their "guests". Despite unleashing the full power of his accursed blood, Mohg is unable to overcome the Tarnished, falling at their hands.

Following his death, Mohg's corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow, where Miquella utilized it for an ancient ritual at the Gate of Divinity. Mohg's body became a vessel to house the revived soul of Radahn, Miquella's promised consort.

sections.heading: Mohg, the Omen
sections.markdown:
Mohg, the Omen** is projection encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, within the Cathedral of the Forsaken that lies beyond the Forsaken Depths Site of Grace. The arena is a fairly small chapel, with pillars on the side that can be used to gain distance. The Dung Eater is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been released from his cell.

Mohg's trident attacks have long delays, and cover a wide range. He uses a number of bloodflame-based attacks, which deal blood loss as well as fire damage. Mohg's Shackle can be used to stun him for a few seconds, allowing for some additional hits.

Defeating **Mohg, the Omen** unlocks the Cathedral of the Forsaken Site of Grace and grants Bloodflame Talons and 100,000 runes. He must be defeated in order to access the Frenzied Flame Proscription.

sections.heading: Mohg, Lord of Blood
sections.markdown:
Mohg, Lord of Blood** is encountered at the top of the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum. The arena is reasonably wide and open, with some gravestones on each side that act as obstacles.

This fight plays out much like the **Mohg, the Omen** fight, until the second phase, when he performs a Bloodboon Ritual and subsequently sprouts enormous black wings. During phase 2, many of Mohg's moveset expands and his attacks will cover large areas in fire.
Mohg, Lord of Blood** must be defeated to unlock the *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* expansion, and enter the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.markdown: Phase 1 is largely the same as the fight against **Mohg, the Omen**. The key difference is the introduction of a countdown. When his health drops to certain levels, he will thrust his spear into the air and chant, causing a red ring to appear around the player. He will do this three times, and once his health reaches 50% he will perform Bloodboon Ritual, dealing huge amounts of damage for each ring and inflicting blood loss, while simultaneously recovering his own health. The Purifying Crystal Tear can be added to the Flask of Wondrous Physick to significantly decrease the amount of damage dealt by this move.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.markdown: After performing Bloodboon Ritual and recovering much of his health, Mohg will sprout wings and his spear will be imbued with bloodflame. The majority of his attacks will spray bloodflame on the ground, leaving patches of fire that last for a long time. He also now has abilities that utilize his wings to get out of range or to close distance easily.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Miquella the Kind**, also known as **Miquella of the Haligtree**, **Empyrean Miquella**, and **the Unalloyed**, is a Remembrance Boss in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is an Empyrean and a son of Queen Marika the Eternal and King Consort Radagon. He is the older twin brother of Malenia, and together they are known as the **Twin Prodigies** (天賦の双子, *Tenpu no Futago*). His other self is St. Trina, whom he divested and cast into the depths of the Stone Coffin Fissure. He is encountered at the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim in the Realm of Shadow, where he fights alongside Radahn, Consort of Miquella.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Miquella and his twin sister were born with incurable afflictions, with Miquella's curse being perpetual youth. Miquella made a promise to Malenia and experimented tirelessly in an attempt to undo their curses. The twins were very close, and Malenia became Miquella's sworn blade and protector. Miquella was loved by many people and had a remarkable ability to compel affection from others. For this reason, many regarded him as the most fearsome Empyrean.

Just as his parents were two halves of the same person, Miquella also had another half—St. Trina—who held the power of Sleep. St. Trina was Miquella's fate, and she was his "love".

Miquella was chosen by his Two Fingers to become an Empyrean, destined to succeed Queen Marika. He was an adherent of Golden Order Fundamentalism, and developed new incantations as gifts to his father Radagon. However, Miquella abandoned Fundamentalism when it failed to treat Malenia's rot. He then began creating Unalloyed Gold, which he used it to craft needles that could ward away the meddling of outer gods and forestall Malenia's incurable rot. These needles could even be used to subdue the power of the Frenzied Flame. He also unsuccessfully sought a solution for his half-brother Godwyn's state of incomplete death.

sections.heading: The Haligtree

At some point, Miquella started watering a sapling with his own blood in the hope that it would become a new Erdtree. The sapling was grown on top of the fortress of Elphael and became known as the Haligtree. Soldiers and Knights sworn to protect the Haligtree would use unalloyed gold to symbolize their loyalty and devotion to Miquella, wearing braided crowns made of the metal and creating shields embedded with it.

Miquella was also said to favor the low and meek, and his Haligtree was intended to be the eventual salvation for the many. It became a hidden haven for the persecuted and the unwanted of the Lands Between, such as the Misbegotten and Albinaurics.

As Miquella pursued godhood, he knew that he would have to take a consort, to which his eyes fell upon his half-brother General Radahn, for he was strong but remained kind. He approached Radahn with his naive offer, to which the General vowed that he would become as such, in return for unspecified terms on Miquella and Malenia's behalf.

Malenia journeyed with her armies to Caelid to confront Radahn. The resulting Battle of Aeonia ended with Malenia unleashing her Scarlet Aeonia, whispering beforehand in Radahn's ear that *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."* After using her last resort attack, Malenia entered a comatose state, and one of her knights took it upon herself to carry her leader's slumbering body back across the Lands Between to the Haligtree. Radahn had survived, albeit barely standing, and his mind was riddled by the Scarlet Rot. He was now little more than a howling beast aimlessly wandering the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike.

Following the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella embedded himself into the Haligtree to progress his ascension, but was kidnapped during his slumber. Another of Miquella's half-brothers was to blame: Mohg, who served an Outer God known as the Formless Mother. He took the sleeping Empyrean deep underground to the Mohgwyn Palace, where he aspired to raise Miquella to full godhood himself through blood offerings, and then to take on the role of Miquella's consort instead of Radahn, becoming the new monarch of a Mohgwyn Dynasty. Mohg urged his followers to render offerings of blood and drench Miquella's cocoon in order to facilitate his awakening.

Despite all of Mohg's efforts, Miquella remained completely unresponsive. At some point, Miquella had covertly placed an enchantment on Mohg, wishing to use the Omen to gain access to the Realm of Shadow. Sir Ansbach, a Pureblood Knight in service to Mohg, attempted to free his lord by challenging Miquella, only to succumb to an enchantment of his own.

Without Miquella's blood offerings, and Malenia no longer protected by her Unalloyed Gold Needle once she was returned, the Haligtree became a misshapen husk. slowly succumbing to the unmitigated Scarlet Rot. Malenia and the Haligtree's soliders desperately awaited Miquella's return to save their rotting home.

sections.heading: The Realm of Shadow
sections.markdown:
Making use of Mohg, Miquella entered the Realm of Shadow, the location of the Gate of Divinity. As Miquella traveled through the Realm of Shadow, he abandoned parts of himself, including his flesh, his eye, his doubt and vacillation, his love, and his fears. Golden Miquella's Crosses resembling a Great Rune appeared at each location where he abandoned something, akin to Miquella's footprints. Miquella's followers, who pursued him into the Realm of Shadow, used these crosses to trace his path through the realm. Miquella also discarded his other half, St. Trina, in the Stone Coffin Fissure. St. Trina, whose love for Miquella was boundless despite her abandonment, recognized that godhood would be a prison for the Empyrean, and desired for him to be killed out of mercy.

Eventually, a Tarnished champion broke into Mohg's palace and slew the Lord of Blood for his great rune. Sir Gideon Ofnir suggested it might be safer to destroy the cocoon that Miquella remains asleep in. Instead, the Tarnished met Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella, who urged them to travel to the Realm of Shadow by touching Miquella's withered arm within the cocoon.

Within the Realm of Shadow, the Tarnished encounters several more of Miquella's followers, learns of his mission to ascend to godhood via the Gate of Divinity, and of the powerful charm that he had placed upon his disciples, which is broken when he discards his Great Rune. After gaining access to the tower of Enir-Ilim, the Tarnished is confronted by a resurrected Radahn, in a vessel made from the remains of Mohg. It is unclear whether Miquella always intended to use Mohg's body to resurrect Radahn. However, he needed a vessel, likely a hornsent or omen one due to their strong connection to the spiritual world, to bind to Radahn's soul. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: Cut Content
sections.markdown:
- In earlier versions of Elden Ring, Miquella was the shardbearer of the Rune of Abundance.
 - In one version, Miquella was associated with the Abundance Twinblade, an item which was later released as Euporia in *Shadow of the Erdtree*.
 - In another build of the game, Miquella's consciousness would have been within the world of his dream. In a cut quest, Miquella acted as *St. Trina of the Cradlesong*, the saint of slumber. He would have sung a lullaby to soothe the Red-Eyed Merchants of their Frenzied Flame affliction and helped them to retain their personhood and prevent them from becoming "one".
- A cutscene associated with Miquella was cut from the final version of Elden Ring., with associated materials including Leaf, Root, Root_Large, Soil_Blood_Stain, Seedling_Blood_vessel, Seedling_Blood_vessel_branch, and Seedling_Blood_vessel_MultColor_branch.
 - There is a cut dialogue most likely associated with this cutscene: *"Young seedling, young seedling. Return to the bosom of earth. But remember well, Thou'rt mine. So shall I give of myself. This is for thee. Mine abundance, my drop of dew. Quench thy thirst, throughout thy frame. Blossom and burgeon, time and and time again. Grow larger, stronger. Until the day cometh. When thou canst share in my dream. Elden Ring, O Elden Ring. Beget Order most elegant, from my tender reverie." *
 - There is a separate dialogue, possibly related to the use of Miquella's Needle: *"If thou covetest the throne, Impress my vision upon thine heart. In the new world of thy making, all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign."*
- There is cut dialogue in which Miquella would have intervened in support of Malenia;
 - The phase one cutscene had her say: *"Sweet Tarnished.. Dearest companion... Did you not heed my warning? Your greed knows no end. You would steal the last drop of warmth from his empty frame? After all you've taken, you still want more? Then you will have to kill me. I am Malenia, Sword of Miquella. And I have never known defeat."*
 - During her second phase cutscene, Miquella would've said: *"My dear twin, accept this gift. A gift of abundance, my last drop of dew. Let all things flourish, whether graceful, or malign."* Presumably, this drop of dew would allow Malenia to ascend to her second phase, and would've been a prerequisite of some kind for Miquella's cut cutscene.
- In Shadow of the Erdtree, there is an unused alternate set of dialogue for the Promised Consort Radahn cutscenes, sandwiched between the retail dialogue internally;
 - Radahn's phase 1 cutscene would have him say: *" I am Radahn. Born of red-maned Radagon, and Rennala of the Full Moon. A lion bred for battle."*
 - The phase 2 cutscene would have had Miquella say: *"I hereby swear. To every living being, and every living soul. Now comes the age of our eden. A thousand year voyage guided by compassion. Beginning here, love encompasses all. No living thing will be denied, no deed censured. I am ready. To embrace the whole of it. Let us go together. Radahn, my promised consort."*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Noble Presence** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Guaranteed Drop:** Volcano Manor
- Noble Presence is acquired by defeating the Godskin Noble found at the Temple of Eiglay on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Noble Presence creates a repelling shockwave that knocks back human-sized enemies within a 1.3-meter radius, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 239% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting a Blackflame effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds.

Charging the spell increases the radius to 2.3 meters and increases the Attack Power to 279% of Incantation Scaling, while also launching human-sized enemies into the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 FP per cast.
- Costs 28 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 36 points.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Deals 16.8 Stance damage. Increases to 21.84 Stance damage when charged.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown:
- The Godskin Noble Robe boosts the effectiveness of this spell by 20%.
- This spell is not strengthened by the Godslayer's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Noble Presence is fairly effective against groups of enemies, as its large area-of-effect shockwave can push back or launch multiple foes at once.
- The knockback effect can be useful in controlling the battlefield by throwing enemies off cliffs or into hazardous areas.
- Can be used defensively to break the Stance of incoming attackers, giving the caster time to heal or reposition.
- Charging the spell for maximum potency is particularly effective against heavier foes and enemies with shields.
- The additional damage from the Blackflame effect is somewhat unreliable, as the invincibility given to launched foes will prevent it from being applied to human-sized foes. It is nonetheless
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Increases Dexterity by 5 and also increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 4%/6%/11%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hits towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive) also increasing the effect.
 - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
 - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia or the Winged Sword Insignia to stack the effect, but only the latter can be obtained in the same playthrough.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
 - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
 - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Misbegotten** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
According to the hornsent, Crucible aspects sprouted on a Giant in the distant past, and its influence would profoundly mark the life forms present in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh

At some point, a group of people would make contact with the Crucible, becoming the Misbegotten, malformed beings that exhibit characteristics of different types of animals, often possessing tails, horns, scales, and wings. They typically have red fur and golden hair. For this act, they would be punished and treated as slaves from birth under the rule of Marika, and their appearance would make them considered impure like Omens. They often wield weighty, iron weapons steeped in resentment.

Misbegotten appear in various regions of the Lands Between. Many found sanctuary in Haligtree Town, situated in the branches of Miquella's Haligtree. Others worship graves and a hooded warrior’s statue in Leyndell, Royal Capital, or guard ancient forges within the Realm of Shadow. A Misbegotten Crusader wields the marital sword forged by Radagon of the Golden Order and leads a group that found refuge in the Cave of the Forlorn. The only friendly Misbegotten is Smithing Master Hewg, a blacksmith cursed by Queen Marika to forge a weapon capable of killing a god. Bound to the Roundtable Hold, he labors endlessly for the Tarnished.

At some point, a population of Misbegotten were employed as slaves at Castle Morne; however, after the Shattering, they rebelled against Godrick's forces stationed there and took over the castle. Castellan Edgar remains behind to ensure the Grafted Blade Greatsword does not fall into the wrong hands. Later, if the Tarnished assists Edgar, a Misbegotten murders Edgar's daughter, Irina of Morne. This drives Edgar to embrace the Frenzied Flame and become a revenger, vowing to avenge his daughter by slaughtering all Misbegotten.

There are four Misbegotten enemy types: cleaver-wielding Misbegotten, bow-wielding Winged Misbegotten, axe-wielding Scaly Misbegotten, and sword-wielding Misbegotten Warriors.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Mt. Gelmir** is a subregion in Elden Ring, located on the Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Description
sections.markdown:
A volcano in western Altus Plateau, which houses the Volcano Manor at its summit. It is characterized by sheer cliffs and ominous skies, qualities which grew more pronounced in the wake of The Shattering.

The dried-up Seethewater River runs along the base of the volcano, with geysers that spew jets of boiling water. The river terminates on the west side, near Fort Laiedd where the forces of Leyndell are locked in conflict with the Fire Monks. The Hermit Village, inhabited by Demi-Humans and Glintstone Sorcerers, sits on the southeastern edge of the volcano. Primeval Sorcerer Azur, one of the founding Glintstone Sorcerers, settled near the village after his banishment from the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Mt. Gelmir was the site of the most horrendous conflict of the Shattering, which has left scars that can still be found. Ruined campsites litter the cliffsides. Some Leyndell Soldiers remain, driven to frenzy by the horrors they saw.

The Volcano Manor, which sits atop the mountain, is the home of the Demigod Praetor Rykard, who once led a company of inquisitors. After the Elden Ring was broken, Rykard fed himself to the blasphemous serpent, Great Rune and all, in defiance of the gods. His knights abandoned him when his noble ambitions were reduced to gluttony and depravity, yet his consort, Tanith, remained by his side. Rykard is now served by the Recusants; a band of Tarnished who hunt their own kind.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Nepheli Loux, Warrior** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked. At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father. Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again, earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.markdown:
At the behest of Gideon, Nepheli infiltrates Stormveil Castle, the home of the demigod Godrick the Grafted. Here, she encounters a Tarnished, who aids her in defeating the decrepit demigod. With Godrick slain, she returns to Roundtable Hold, where she awards them with an Arsenal Charm she found in Stormveil, and encourages them to speak to her foster father.

Travelling to Liurnia of the Lakes, Nepheli comes upon the Village of the Albinaurics, where she witnesses the slaughter of the Albinauric inhabitants at the hands of her father's men. Reminded of the brutality she witnessed as a child, Nepheli vows to deliver justice to the oppressors, assisting the Tarnished in defeating the Omenkiller responsible for the slaughter.

For giving into her emotions and abandoning the mission, Nepheli is cast aside by Gideon. Without her estranged father's guidance, she becomes crestfallen, resigning to the lower levels of Roundtable Hold where she questions the faith she had in Gideon.

The Tarnished obtains the ashes of The Stormhawk King in the Chapel of Anticipation, which they may choose to give to Nepheli. She can smell the ancient storm within the ash, and is reminded of her first hawk. Despite her inability to sense spirits within ash, she gladly receives them.

After claiming the Stormhawk King's ashes, Nepheli encounters Kenneth Haight, who recognises her as a worthy heir of Limgrave. Nepheli accepts the role, having been reminded by Limgrave of her own home. As the new lord of Limgrave, Nepheli pledges to aid the Tarnished should they become Elden Lord, pledging to call upon the storm to drive away the foulness that has settled on the winds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Millicent** is an NPC cooperator in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Millicent is a red-haired woman afflicted by Scarlet Rot. She and her sisters were found in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid by Sage Gowry, who raised them as his daughters. Her four sisters travelled to Miquella's Haligtree under Gowry's guidance, however Millicent alone remained behind.

At Gowry's behest, the Tarnished obtains an Unalloyed Gold Needle and brings it to the Church of the Plague, where Millicent is slowly succumbing to the Rot. She inserts the needle to stall the Rot, regaining her strength. However, her memories appear to have been affected by her sickness, as when she struggles to remember Gowry upon returning to his shack to find it abandoned.

Millicent sets off on a journey across the Lands Between, retracing the route taken by Malenia, Blade of Miquella after the battle of Aeonia. She once again meets the Tarnished on the Altus Plateau, where they present her with a Valkyrie's Prosthesis to replace her missing sword arm.

Millicent's journey takes her to the Mountaintops of the Giants, in search of a fort containing a medallion which will allow her to access the Haligtree. After the Tarnished claims the medallion and travels to the Consecrated Snowfield, Millicent makes her way to the Haligtree, and to Elphael, the city at its base. Here, she reveals to the Tarnished that she is of Malenia's blood, although she is unsure whether she is a sister, daughter, or offshoot of the Demigod. Unbeknownst to Millicent, however, the Tarnished has been advised by Gowry to assist his remaining four daughters in killing Millicent, so that she can be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

The Tarnished may then make a choice: kill Millicent alongside her four sisters, or fight alongside her against the attackers. Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, she will become a scarlet aeonia flower, waiting for Malenia's ascension. If the player fights alongside her, she will remove the needle from her body, allowing her to succumb to the Rot.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Mountaintops of the Giants** is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The northern Mountaintops were once the home of the Fire Giants, after they claimed them from the Ice Dragons. At the birth of the Erdtree, the forces of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, First Elden Lord marched up the mountain and put the Giants to the sword. With the Giants defeated, the Flame of Ruin was confined within the Giants' Forge atop the mount, and the Age of the Erdtree began.

The Fire Monks, who were left behind to watch over the Flame of Ruin, can be found patrolling the region. They are often accompanied by the Guilty: thorn sorcerers who were banished to the north. Their fortress, the Guardians' Garrison, sits on the eastern side of the mountain.

The Zamor Ruins in the southwest are the home of an ancient clan of Zamor Warriors. They were ancient enemies of the Fire Giants, and are regarded as heroes due to their actions in the War Against the Giants.

The Mountaintops were also home to the astrologers, neighbors of the Giants and predecessors to the modern Glintstone Sorcerers. The ruins of their civilization can be found in the central Mountaintops.

The northernmost section of the Mountaintops is dominated by Castle Sol, where the site of an eclipse once inspired dreadful awe. Half of a medallion that will grant access to Miquella's Haligtree can be found here, protected by Commander Niall.

The medallion can be used at the Grand Lift of Rold to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield, which sprawls to the west of the Mountaintops. The Albinaurics, and others who revere Miquella, seek this sacred land in the hopes of earning the Empyrean's favour. Ordina, Liturgical Town is the final stop on the way to the Haligtree, and is home to several Albinauric Archers.

sections.markdown: Nokron, Eternal City** is a subregion in Elden Ring, located along the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Nokron is one of the Eternal Cities of the Nox, who were banished underground after invoking the ire of the Greater Will. Nokron's chair-crypt houses the Fingerslayer Blade, a blood-drenched fetish made from a corpse that can harm the Greater Will and its vassals, and is proof of the treason of the Nox.

Nokron is notably difficult to access. Long ago, a band of slaves-turned-soldiers called the Fallen Hawks were ordered to explore the Eternal Cities. Although they managed to find their way into the subterranean realm, they became trapped after they discovered the Ghostflame. While the city is visible from the lower portion of Siofra River, the route to it is only opened after Starscourge Radahn is defeated, which causes a star to fall upon Limgrave, opening a deep crater near Fort Haight.

sections.markdown: The **Mohgwyn Palace** is a subregion in Elden Ring. It is located on an island in the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
An island in the underground Siofra River, far to the east of Nokron, Eternal City. The grave of an ancient dynasty civilization can be found here, and it is in these ruins that Mohg, Lord of Blood, has chosen to be the seat of his coming Mohgwyn Dynasty.

A large part of the area is taken up by a blood-red lake, which is the habitat of many abominations. The Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum juts out of the west side of the island, housing the Lord of Blood and his vassals.

There are two possible entrances to this area. The conventional route is via a sending gate on the western edge of Consecrated Snowfield, which leads to a cliff on the southeastern side of the palace. Alternately, by becoming a Pureblood Knight of the Mohgwyn Dynasty, one can obtain a Pureblood Knight's Medal from White Mask Varré, which will teleport the player to the mausoleum entrance at will.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Miquella's Haligtree** (ミケラの聖樹, *Mikera no Seiju*) is a legacy dungeon located north of the Consecrated Snowfield. It is accessible after solving the puzzle in the Evergaol at Ordina, Liturgical Town and taking the Sending Gate.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Miquella's Haligtree is a vast, misshapen tree in the far north of the Lands Between. Built into the canopy is Haligtree Town, a sanctuary for the unwanted. At the base of the tree is Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, a city largely inhabited by the Haligtree Knights and Cleanrot Knights who serve Miquella and Malenia. Both areas contain statues of the twin Demigods.

Long ago, the Empyrean Miquella abandoned Golden Order Fundamentalism after realizing it could not treat Malenia's Scarlet Rot. He sought to establish an Unalloyed Gold order away from the Erdtree and settled on the Haligtree. Miquella watered the sapling with his own Empyrean blood, and later wove a cocoon and embedded himself within its trunk to nurture it directly. However, it would fail to grow into an Erdtree. Before he could finish, Miquella was cut and taken from the tree by Mohg, who was under his charm. The Lord of Blood zealously wished to raise the Empyrean to godhood and become his consort. After returning from her battle with Radahn, Malenia awaited her brother's return at the base of the tree, and over time infected the tree with her Scarlet Rot.

Nevertheless, the Haligtree and its city became a haven for those rejected by society, such as the Misbegotten and the Kindred of Rot. Loretta, a former Knight of Caria, founded a sanctuary for Albinaurics among the boughs of the Haligtree. Those who made the pilgrimage presented a secret medallion at the Grand Lift of Rold to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield. They traveled north and crossed the river to Ordina, Liturgical Town, where they journeyed through a Sending Gate.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- While the skill, Sacred Blade, is excellent, at this point of the game most bosses and tough enemies are resistant to Holy damage, and most tough Those Who Live in Death will have been defeated, making it far less useful than the much earlier acquisition of Ash of War: Sacred Blade is.
- Has a unique heavy attack that causes the user to step forward. This attack has good forward reach, and since the first attack in the charged version makes a short dash forward it's useful to catch opponents out of their roll and for landing the Stance-breaking charged heavy attack while not having to stand too close to enemies.
- This weapon gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, as the Faith-scaling is mostly useful for increasing the damage of the Skill.
 - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 605 AP, 80 Strength or Dexterity grants 581 AP, 45 Strength (or Dexterity) and 45 Faith grants 566 AP, and 80 Faith grants 516 AP.
 - In other words, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity is best if looking to maximize AP while 45 Strength and 45 Faith (Strength is slightly preferable over Dexterity due to the bonus from two-handing) is better for a mix of attack damage and skill damage.
- Pairs surprisingly well with the Golden Epitaph, another Holy sword that scales similarly well on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity or Strength/Faith build.
